title: Cross-Pool Skill Bank & WeekZero Delegation Manual (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working manual for rapidly spinning up temporary role coverage from adjacent teams using a lightweight skill bank. Goal: reduce time-to-cover for short-term gaps (1–8 weeks), preserve product momentum, and create clear evidence for conversion or permanent hire decisions.

Scope & applicability:
- Use when a role is: on immediate leave, has a short unplanned vacancy, or during recruiter velocity pauses and interview backlogs.
- Suitable for IC-level roles through senior IC; for manager coverage, follow the separate manager-shadow protocol.
- Not intended for permanent hiring decisions (use hiring pipeline).

Core principles:
1) Minimum viable continuity: restore critical flow for the top 2 team priorities fast, not full feature parity.
2) Explicit timeboxes: clear start/end, conversion assessment windows.
3) Low-friction delegation: template-driven handoffs, checklists, and 1:1 shadowing blocks.
4) Measurement: track 3 KPIs during coverage to enable objective conversion/ramp decisions.

Quick glossary:
- Skill Bank: a curated list of adjacent ICs with surface-level capabilities and availability windows.
- WeekZero: the first 5 working days of coverage focusing on triage, context capture, and immediate delivery.
- Coverage Slate: the set of tasks/owners for the coverage period.

WeekZero checklist (day-by-day guidance):
Day 0 (pre-start, ideally <24h)
- Notify the skill-bank volunteer and manager + calendar hold.
- Share minimal context packet: product area README, current sprint board link, 3 priority tickets, access instructions.
- Set explicit goals for WeekZero: what “good enough” looks like.

Day 1
- 30m alignment with team manager: scope narrow-down (stop doing list), deliverables, & critical SLAs.
- 1h walk-through of codebase/doc links or product mockups; pair on the highest-priority ticket.
- Add volunteer to Slack channel and signal responsibilities publicly.

Day 2–3
- Volunteer owns triage of top 3 tickets; manager reviews PRs daily with focused feedback (30m).
- Start an evidence log: list decisions, blocked items, time spent per task.
- Schedule a 1-hour deep-dive with subject-matter owner if needed.

Day 4–5
- Close or progress tickets to behind-PR/merged state where feasible.
- Draft a short retrospective note documenting coverage success, outstanding risk, and recommended next steps (convert, extend, hire).
- Manager and volunteer sign off on WeekZero completion.

Coverage slate template (to paste in a ticket or doc):
- Role covered: [role title]
- Coverage dates: [start — end]
- Top 2 priorities (what must not break):
  - P1: [short phrase]
  - P2: [short phrase]
- Things NOT to do: [stop list]
- Volunteer: [name + manager contact]
- Escalation path: [pager/SLACK-channel] -> [backup person]
- Acceptance criteria for each priority (short bullets)
- Handoff artifacts location: [confluence / drive link]

Volunteer selection guidance (skill-bank maintenance):
- Volunteers are nominated by managers quarterly. Each entry in the bank includes: level alignment (IC2, IC3, etc.), surface skills, recent relevant projects, and typical availability windows.
- Prioritize volunteers with adjacent domain familiarity and strong cross-team communication history.
- For stretch coverage (outside comfort zone), pair the volunteer with a subject expert for the first 48 hours.

Operational guardrails & policies:
- Maximum continuous coverage length without formal conversion interview: 8 weeks. If coverage must exceed 8 weeks, initiate a hiring cadence or formal internal conversion interview within week 6.
- Overtime limits: volunteers should not exceed 20% of normal weekly capacity during coverage unless explicitly agreed and compensated via time-off-in-lieu.
- Compensation note: track volunteer time against manager OKR credits (people-ops ledger) for equitable load distribution.

Conversion evidence rubric (used at the end of coverage):
- Delivery: completed acceptance criteria for P1 and P2 (Yes/No).
- Ramp speed: arrival-to-first-PR-time (target <72h).
- Code quality / peer review feedback: number of rework cycles; qualitative note.
- Cross-team communication: stakeholder satisfaction (1–5).
- Desire & fit: volunteer’s interest in permanent move (yes/no/unknown).
Use these signals to decide: convert (hire internally), extend (short window), or create req to external hire.

Sample manager email to volunteer (pasteable):
Subject: Quick thank-you + weekzero plan for covering [role]
Hi [Volunteer],
Thanks again for stepping in. Below is the compressed plan for WeekZero:
- Start: [date/time]
- Top priorities: [P1], [P2]
- Key access: [repo link], [prod-dashboard], [slack channel]
- Expectation: triage P1/P2, keep a short evidence log, and draft a 1-paragraph conclusion by end of day 5.
I’ll review PRs each day at 3pm. Reach out to [SME] for domain questions.
—[manager]

Evidence log template (one-line per item):
[YYYY-MM-DD] [ticket]: action taken — time spent — blockers/resolution — stakeholder note

KPI dashboard markers (for people-ops to track during coverage):
- Mean days to first meaningful commit
- % P1 acceptance at week end
- Volunteer-reported cognitive load (1–5)
- Stakeholder satisfaction (1–5)

Failure modes & mitigations:
- Volunteer blocked by missing access: escalate to infra owner, use temporary read-only snapshots for triage.
- Volunteer overloaded: cut scope to P1 only + ask for extra volunteer.
- Coverage causing product regressions: stop new changes, switch to read-only patching and escalate to SRE.

Post-coverage artifacts (what to save):
- Signed WeekZero completion note (manager + volunteer).
- Evidence log saved to role folder.
- Short hiring recommendation (convert/extend/open-req) with reasons.
- If internal conversion recommended, include conversion interview slate (role-specific probe list).

Appendix: short example of conversion interview probes (for engineering IC)
- Walk me through the most important change you made during coverage; what tradeoffs did you evaluate?
- How would you onboard a replacement to prevent this gap repeating?
- Which design in the codebase felt surprising and why?
- Show a brief code walk: what would you change with more time?

Notes / open questions (WIP):
- How granular should manager credits be for volunteer time? (Samir to propose ledger approach).
- Should volunteers get a formal micro-bonus vs. time-off? (discussion needed with finance).
- Can we automate a ‘coverage’ label in Jira and auto-add volunteers to PR reviewers? (linked ticket: JIRA-HR-1427).

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Samir: propose ledger credit model by 2025-11-20.
- Lucia: draft volunteer nomination cadence and template by 2025-11-10.
- Avery: pilot two cross-pool covers in Nov 2025 and collect KPI snapshot.

End of document.
